keyRules: Maximum altitude: 120 m (400 ft) above ground level, in uncontrolled airspace.
Minimum distance of 8 km from any airport or aerodrome; flying closer requires DGAC approval and the issuance of a NOTAM.

Fly only away from congested areas of buildings in cities, towns or settlements and away from open-air gatherings of people. Only with specific DGAC approval may you operate closer, and never closer than 30 m to those buildings or gatherings.
ALL drones weighing less than 25 kg must have an identification plate with the serial number, owner's name, and phone number
Mandatory registration at drones.dgac.go.cr: drones ≥25 kg and all non-recreational use (commercial or non-commercial), regardless of weight
Recreational use <25 kg: Does NOT require formal registration if you follow basic rules
Always keep the drone within direct line of sight (VLOS)
Flying is permitted only during the day and in good weather—night flying requires authorization
Non-recreational, non-commercial use (including drones <25 kg): DGAC certificate of competence (min. 18 years old), civil liability insurance and registration at drones.dgac.go.cr
Commercial use: RPAS license + Technical Council certificate + DGAC operational certificate
It is prohibited to fly over private property without permission, prisons, restricted areas, and airports
importantNotes: 🏷️ MANDATORY IDENTIFICATION PLATE: Although drones weighing less than 25 kg for recreational use do NOT require formal registration, ALL drones must have an identification plate with a serial number, the owner’s name, and a contact phone number. This is the strictest requirement for physical identification.

✈️ FOREIGN TOURISTS: The rules apply to non-residents. For recreational use: identification plate + follow basic rules (no airports, no private property, no prisons) — no formal registration required. Customs may request a drone declaration upon entry into the country. Foreign pilots for commercial purposes: the DGAC may validate a foreign RPAS license (license and medical certificate must be valid) for a maximum of 3 months, renewable only once for 3 months in justified cases. Validation does not replace the other requirements for commercial use.
🌳 NATIONAL PARKS AND SINAC: drones are not permitted in Manuel Antonio National Park (SINAC). Other protected areas may prohibit or restrict them — check with each area BEFORE your trip.

🏖️ RESTRICTED ZONES: without DGAC permission, flying is prohibited in prohibited or restricted zones published in the AIP and within 8 km of airports such as SJO and LIR. Also check for possible municipal restrictions.

💰 COMMERCIAL USE AND PENALTIES: Commercial flights without an RPAS license or a certificate from the Technical Council may result in fines, confiscation of equipment, and a ban on operations. For paid photography/video work: obtain the license before beginning the activity.

fields.disclaimerText: Always check the DGAC’s official sources before flying. This app is a tool, not a legal authority. Costa Rica enforces the RAC-RPAS (Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44615-MOPT, in force since 27/09/2024). All drones must have an identification plate; commercial use requires a certificate from the Civil Aviation Technical Council.
